summary: William Joseph Wilkins was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Highgate School and Hackney College. He served as a teacher at Bhowanipore Missionary Institution and at Bhownipur College for the London Missionary Society from circa 1865 to 1884.

William Knighton worked in the fields of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as headmaster at the Norman Seminary in Colombo (ca. 1845–1850), Lecturer in History and Logic at Presidency University in 1846, and held a post in the Indian Civil Service.

William L. Ames is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who earned an M.S. at Caltech and a Ph.D. at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Collett Cox. His career includes posts at CIIS and JFK University.

William Lee-Warner worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Rugby School and St John's College (B.A. 1865–1869), he served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1869 to 1895 and was a Fellow of the University of Mumbai.

William Linwood was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Christ Church, Oxford (B.A. 1836–1839, M.A. ca. 1835–1842). He taught at Shrewsbury School and served as a public examiner at the University of Oxford in 1850.

William Logan worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Edinburgh, he served in the Madras Civil Service from 1862 to 1888 and became a Fellow of the University of Madras in 1882.

William M. Bodiford is a Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale (Ph.D. under Stanley Weinstein), he taught at Davidson, Iowa, and UCLA, retiring as Professor Emeritus in 2023.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Connecticut College and an M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia (completed 2006), where he was supervised by David Germano.
William MacColin Kirkpatrick was an Indology scholar who was educated at Bishop Cotton School and served in the Indian Civil Service.

William Markby worked in Indology and law. Educated at Merton College and Oxford (D.C.L.), he served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1877–1878) and Oxford's Reader in Indian Law (1878–1900), holding fellowships at Balliol and All Souls.

William McCulloch was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He was educated at Royal High School, George Watson's College, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the University of Edinburgh, later serving as Principal of Chinsurah Theological College in 1886.

William McGrath is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his MA-PhD at the University of Virginia (2010–2017). After affiliations with the University of Virginia, he became an Assistant Professor at New York University in 2021.

William Montgomery McGovern was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned a D.Phil. from Christ Church, Oxford. He lectured at SOAS (1918–1924) and served as Professor of Far Eastern Studies at Northwestern University from 1929.

William Nassau Lees was an Indologist, linguist, and historian educated at Trinity College Dublin. He served as Secretary to the Board of Examiners at Fort William around 1855 and as Principal and Professor at Aliah University from circa 1855 to 1870.

William P. Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. in 2006 at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Pettigrew was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Ardington Aborigines Mission Training Centre from circa 1888 to 1890 and served as a missionary for the American Baptist Missionary Union beginning in 1894.

William Price was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as interpreter on Gore Ouseley's Mission to Persia (1811–1812) and taught at Fort William College, becoming Professor of Hindee and Hindoostanee in 1824.

William R. Hutchison was a religious studies and history scholar. Educated at Oxford and Yale (Ph.D. 1956), he held posts at Yale, Hunter College, American University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and began teaching at Harvard University in 1968.

William R. LaFleur was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who held degrees from Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago (Ph.D.). He held faculty posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania (1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper was a linguist and religious studies scholar. After doctoral studies at Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he taught at Yale and Baptist Union Theological Seminary, served as President of Bradley University, and was President of the University of Chicago (1891–1906).
